1935.statement: Printed subsection 'Of Marriage, whether it shall take effect or no?' begins below the Alkindus aphorisms on original PDF337 and continues PDF338.
1935.limit: It has a printed heading, although it is not a new numbered chapter.

1941.statement: Lilly's alternatives include first lord in seventh, seventh lord in ascendant, or aspecting the LORD of the opposite house by good aspect; each gives encouragement for effecting the match.
1941.precondition: The first or seventh significator must occupy the counterpart's house OR behold the appropriate lord with favourable aspect.
1941.limit: Do not collapse 'in seventh' into any unspecified 'other house'; the phrase 'or with the Lord thereof' is preserved.

1948.statement: Mutual/interchangeable dignities, reception, translation or collection by a weightier planet may perfect marriage; the passage describes these as additional source testimonies.
1948.precondition: Actual dignity exchange or light/reception mechanism involving relevant signifiers.
1948.limit: The source does not require prior failure of every simple aspect; previous draft added an unsupported exclusion.

1952.statement: Seventh lord in seventh, especially its own domicile, describes the desired partner as free from love, little minded to marry, and with the woman's or man's marriage portion known.
1952.precondition: Lord of seventh in seventh or own domicile as printed.
1952.limit: Both source ideas, freedom from love and portion known, are authorial guesses not actual wishes or finances.

1964.statement: The marriage may be broken on the QUERENT'S behalf when funds or fortune are lacking ON THAT SIDE, where the obstructing planet is lord of second.
1964.precondition: Second-house lord actually hinders the significators' reception; lack of money is attributed to querent's side.
1964.limit: Do not infer insufficient dowry of the quesited here; the text locates the deficiency on querent's side.

1965.statement: Third-lord obstruction is attributed to the querent's kindred, brother, sister, untoward neighbour or a journey.
1965.precondition: Third lord participates as frustrating planet in the marriage question.
1965.limit: The source says 'some Journey', not necessarily a short journey.

1966.statement: Fourth-lord hindrance may indicate a parent refusing to agree, inability/refusal to part with lands/houses/tenements, or a parent who WILL SETTLE NO ESTATE.
1966.precondition: Fourth-house lord is the obstruction; parent/property categories are alternatives.
1966.limit: Original says 'will settle no Estate', a refusal rather than demonstrated inability.

1968.statement: Sixth-house hindrance can arise from the querent's father's kindred, an uncle or a servant, or illness affecting the querent.
1968.limit: Keep the source's 'his Fathers Kinred' and alternatives; no medical assessment inferred.

1970.statement: Eighth-lord as marriage impediment can mean death bereaves the QUERENT before marriage, or that the QUESITED lacks sufficient portion and their estate is disapproved.
1970.precondition: Eighth lord is obstructing; distinguish the affected querent and quesited parties.
1970.limit: The author presents two outcomes; the record does not independently establish inheritance, an actual death, or deficient wealth.

1971.statement: Ninth-lord impediment can mean the QUESITED'S kindred, religious difference or an obstinate priest, or a long journey undertaken by the QUERENT.
1971.precondition: Ninth lord is the frustrating significator.
1971.limit: The identities and who undertakes the journey are explicit and must not be reversed.

1974.statement: Twelfth-lord obstruction suggests secret underhand dealings and slander against the QUERENT, who Lilly says may NEVER KNOW by whom the slander was privately insinuated.
1974.precondition: Twelfth lord actually obstructs the match.
1974.limit: Source speculation; do not attribute actual secret slander to an unidentified real person.

1986.limit: Plurality-of-husbands passage uses Sun and Mars wording associated with original-volume erratum printed307 line28 'r for [Sun glyph] and [Mars glyph]'. Body glyph is partially obscured and source-collation uncertainty remains.

1996.statement: Lilly's preferred way to compare spouses' alleged nobility is ESSENTIAL DIGNITY first, then, if no advantage there, WHO IS BEST PLACED IN AN ANGLE; he says same method compares companions or other persons.
1996.precondition: Compare relevant two significators' essential dignity first; use angularity only if that does not decide.
1996.limit: Historical class hierarchy not valid social worth; prior draft treated dignity and angularity as equal simultaneous criteria and omitted 'two Companions'.

1998.statement: When ascendant lord or Moon is received at an angle by a heavy/ponderous planet under the printed reception conditions, Lilly says THE QUERENT SHALL BE MASTER; other strength/dignity placements may indicate submission.
1998.precondition: First lord or Moon received by appropriate weighty angular planet; consider relative dignity/house placement.
1998.limit: Source's power inference is period social ideology, not relationship compatibility evidence.

2003.statement: When a woman asks about a man's wealth, Lilly says to judge in the same manner and concerning HER estate as printed ('ead em est ratio' in Latin is given), without specifying an additional modern turned-house algorithm.
2003.precondition: Woman herself asks the financial question; apply the text's stated analogy.
2003.limit: Printed wording 'of her estate' is copy-qualified; earlier draft silently changed the person to man and invented a turned-house procedure.
